A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ParEVO. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained figures, tables, equations and examples can be matched despite substantial relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-generation benchmarks, runtime and scaling measurements, evolutionary-agent ablations, and code-generation case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds token-matched fine-tuning comparisons, search-strategy ablations, and training-data integrity and overlap analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the reported ECA verification procedure from dynamic race detection to repeated stress tests rejecting timeouts or inconsistent outputs. It also replaces MAP-Elites descriptors based on code length, cyclomatic complexity and synchronization frequency with character length and mean Levenshtein distance. These revise central verification and search components, rather than merely explaining them.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds actual fine-tuning on filtered HPC-Instruct OpenMP examples. Table 2 removes the Plane Sweep evaluation, with no corresponding result retained elsewhere. The principal ParEval, PBBSBench, RPB and DMOJ coverage remains.

E2.justification: New evaluated comparators include DeepSeek-OMP in Table 7 and Best-of-N, Best-of-N plus CoT, and Self-Refine in Table 8, alongside additional ECA variants. Table 5 also adds GPT-5 Thinking and Claude Opus 4.5 to the OpenMP comparison, where neither participated in v1.

E3.justification: Tables 1 and 5 add geometric-mean speedups, including an outlier-exclusion evaluation using a 32× threshold. New experiments introduce a matched 2.14-million-token training budget and 5/15/30-iteration controls. Section 3.3 revises candidate validation to large-input stress testing. These extend and revise the evaluation design; they do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's iteration ablation and retained case studies, v2 tests abstraction choice under matched training tokens, alternative search strategies, diversity removal, and fine-tuning/search synergy. Appendices H–I add manual test-integrity checks, a ThreadSanitizer audit and training–evaluation overlap analysis; Table 5 adds outlier sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: v2 first specifies five repeated stress-test executions per candidate and checks output consistency across them. This adds repeat-count information, without establishing an increase over v1's actual runs. No new benchmark confidence intervals, significance tests or random-seed reporting accompany the added comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 5 extensively revise reported scores: DeepSeek-Parlay's speedup changes from 16.40 to 126.16, GPT-5 Thinking's from 14.03 to 0.43, and Gemini-2.5-Parlay's Pass@1 from 0.33 to 0.58. v2 also adds geometric-mean results and Tables 7–9, while removing Plane Sweep results. These are revised reported outcomes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 introduces a different quantitative definition of archive diversity: mean character-level Levenshtein distance to other population members. The compile-and-test acceptance condition and inverse-runtime fitness equations remain unchanged, and no theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its description of the correctness contribution by removing dynamic race detectors from the ECA feedback claim. The central contributions—Parlay-Instruct, specialized models, evolutionary refinement and the correctness–speedup trade-off—and the broad performance-superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces blanket improvements in compilation and correctness with category-dependent gains and regressions, and explains the headline mean through heavy-tailed algorithmic speedups. Section 4.4 adds a contention-based explanation of scaling degradation. New appendices interpret token efficiency, diversity, fine-tuning synergy, test integrity and leakage, substantially expanding the scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 discloses synthesis passes, 29,700 initial candidates and 15,880 rejections; explains seed-test reuse and the validation-only role of the 700 held-out tasks; and documents audit procedures. Appendix E supplies OpenMP filtering steps, token budget and additional LoRA settings. These materially expand reproducibility information; the existing code and model access links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused discussions of ML compiler optimization and execution-feedback synthesis, citing works such as CompilerGym, MLGO, Ansor, InterCode and LEVER. These extend the positioning around abstraction level and runtime feedback while retaining the original research framing. Publication and bibliographic updates to existing references are not new related works.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract, rewrites the results interpretation, shortens discussion and conclusion passages, and updates author and publication information. It adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements and reorganizes appendix headings, while preserving the main section order and much of the existing prose.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 expand from single-column to full-width displays, and Tables 1 and 5 gain metric columns. Three new tables are added. Training examples, category plots and the semantic-alignment example move into reorganized appendices; the workflow diagram replaces Race Detection with Stress Testing. Many remaining appendix figures are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the evidence more informative through matched-training controls, search ablations, data audits and geometric-mean/outlier reporting, while correcting v1's blanket interpretation of correctness gains. The net improvement is limited by unexplained large score revisions and overinterpretation of new evidence: Table 9 includes a substantially faster no-diversity result despite generalized claims about diversity preventing local optima. Replacing the stated dynamic-race-detector filter with stress testing also leaves weaker support for concurrency-safety assurances.
